title: Retry loop has no upper bound
summary: LoginClient.retry retries every 5xx response with no attempt limit. During an outage the client loops until the user leaves the screen.
explanation: LoginClient wraps the sign-in request. On a 5xx it waits (exponential backoff, capped at 8 s) and sends the request again. Nothing counts attempts, so a long outage produces a request every 8 s per open client, and the spinner never ends.
severityRationale: Medium. No data loss, but every stuck client adds load to an already failing service, and the user sees an endless spinner.

sources.excerpt: This retry never stops on repeated 503s.

research.analysis: The loop at LoginClient.swift:92 runs while status >= 500. Backoff exists; an attempt cap does not.

options.title: Cap at 3 attempts
options.description: Add maxAttempts = 3 and surface the last error to the caller.

options.title: Cap from remote config
options.description: Read the cap from a config flag, default 3.
cons: Adds a flag to create and maintain

options.title: Shared retry policy for all clients
options.description: Move every client onto one RetryPolicy type.
pros: Fixes the same bug in 6 other clients

options.title: Leave as is
options.description: The gateway sheds load during outages.
cons: Client still loops if the gateway is unreachable

triage.complexityReason: One guard and one test in a single file.
triage.confidenceReason: Cap is clearly right; only the exact number is a preference.

entries.question: Do other clients have the same loop?
entries.answer: Yes, 6 others copy this loop. Added option C (defer a shared RetryPolicy).

entries.question: Would option A change what the user sees?
entries.answer: After the third failure the screen shows the existing generic error instead of spinning.
